I have worked this land since I was a small girl, and my mother taught me how to care for the trees. I do not buy fertilizer from the shop in town because one bag costs too much and I have never used it on these trees. I plant local cassava between the trees using cuttings I save from last year, and I do not spray anything because poison costs money and I do not trust it. We wait for the rains; there is no water here for irrigation. My daughter and my grandchildren will come to help me weed and pick the nuts, so we will spend many days working together. I will not hire workers from outside because I do not have cash to pay them.
